prediction.likelyOutcome: The University is very likely to prevail on its $1,475,000 unpaid-rent counterclaim and to have the June 2013 termination of the Ground Lease upheld, given the Developer's repeated, admitted, deliberate nonpayment across three extended deadlines and four notices of default; the Developer's competing breach/declaratory-judgment claims and eight-figure damages theories are unlikely to succeed given the weight of the trial record on the good-faith negotiation issue. The principal practical caveat is collectibility: the named Developer LLC appears to be judgment-proof, making CastleRock's continuing exposure and any settlement leverage over possession of the Property more important than the paper judgment amount.

outcome.description: After an eight-day bench trial the court entered judgment for the University on its counterclaim and third-party complaint and against the Developer on its claim: the University's termination of the Ground Lease and Development Agreement was effective and a permissible forfeiture of all of the Developer's rights, and the University was awarded damages of $1,475,000 (the unpaid second rent installment, exactly its counterclaim demand), with interest and fees in an amount to be determined on a later submission. The Developer's claimed damages (leasehold $14.4M, delay $4.1M, lost tax abatement $6.2M) were not awarded. No appeal is reflected in the opinion.
outcome.finalNote: No appeal reflected in the opinion text (subsequent history not otherwise checked). Interest and contractual fees were left to a later submission and are not stated, so attorneysFeesAtTrial is null; the non-monetary forfeiture of the Developer's ground-lease rights is not valued in the amount.
